request_flow.summary: Lock the Purchase, revalidate actor and Privacy authority, rebuild S1's accepted snapshot and reject a paid or changed source.
Bind the reference to the existing Purchase.attempt_id. Commit the claim in a separate transaction and read the exact epoch and reference through an unboxed PostgreSQL connection before sending.
Only the claim winner enters the fixed Req path. Store the fixture code or encrypted TEST capability under the same claim and check payer authority before presentation.

guards: Exact integration and environment. A provider attempt requires runtime approval bound to this attempt ID.
side_effects: Persist a stable reference and accepted snapshot digest.
Commit the only claim ID. Failed or uncertain acknowledgements leave the claim intact.
WELL-219 binds the local Verify listener and persists the first due time with the claim.

guards: Canonical capability URL and matching code for the exact integration
side_effects: Retain a fixture code or an authenticated encrypted provider capability once. The current payer can recover the original URL.

security_invariants.summary: The recipient may observe the S1 purchase and still lack initiation and capability recovery authority. Current canonical payer and Privacy checks apply at both boundaries.

Wire code compiles only in TEST. The real integration has a fixed HTTPS origin. Its local seam pins the exact loopback certificate. Fixture credentials, origins, retention and Verify schedules cannot cross into provider scope.
Emit only response classifications and timings. Reject provider dispatch when Finch handlers could capture raw metadata. Mark the reference and capability sensitive and hide them from inspection.
A bound hosted attempt cannot accept synthetic P1/S1 evidence. Separate unbound fixtures retain qualified synthetic behavior. Initialize does not verify payment or grant a right.

concurrency.summary: The Purchase lock serializes dispatch admission and the existing synthetic application path. Private claim and retention updates filter on the unconsumed or matching epoch respectively.

The action rejects explicit outer transactions and reads the exact claim from a different unboxed connection. This also excludes an implicit SQL Sandbox savepoint. The receiver counts actual POSTs independently.

idempotency_retry.summary: Exact replay recovers the original reference. A committed claim remains consumed after a lost response, timeout, error envelope or application restart.
Req uses HTTP/1, disables retries and redirects, bounds pool/connect/receive and best-effort exchange times, and caps the response body at 16 KiB.

failure_recovery.summary: Pre-commit rollback preserves the original prepared reference for its first dispatch. After commitment the claim is ambiguous until applicable evidence is retained, even when the receiver saw no request.
A fresh BEAM recovers the committed capability without another send. An unreadable or missing capability leaves the original claim ambiguous.
The additive schema leaves P1, S1 and E2a rows intact. Rollback holds an exclusive table lock and refuses to erase a retained binding.

safe_extensions.summary: Actual provider operation requires exact WELL-176 owner approval and applicable stage evidence. Bind runtime NEW_YOU_PAYSTACK_TEST_ENABLED, NEW_YOU_PAYSTACK_TEST_APPROVED_ATTEMPT_ID, NEW_YOU_PAYSTACK_TEST_RESTRICTED_KEY, NEW_YOU_PAYSTACK_TEST_EMAIL and NEW_YOU_PAYSTACK_TEST_CAPABILITY_KEY (base64, 32 decoded bytes). Supply secret values privately and preserve the capability key for recovery.

reuse.summary: EXTEND the PR #312 matrix with the reviewed draft Store PR #234 head cdb56c61137bd27d4c13bcb66941611792b2b5f5. Adapt checkout_payload and request in lib/store/payments/providers/paystack.ex, the checkout envelope from lib/store/payments/providers/paystack/response.ex, non-idempotent request settings from lib/store/support/http/req_client.ex, and exact-payload and reference-mismatch cases from test/store/payments/providers/paystack_checkout_test.exs. NewYou uses the locked Req 0.7.5 stack and an actual Bandit loopback receiver.

COMPOSE Store main 949821ac589addb6e595f6333370ed65cf8d5ef7, lib/store/subscriptions/renewal_collection_attempts.ex, claim_dispatch_locked, ensure_exact_dispatch_epoch and claim_collection_dispatch. Use Commerce-owned filtered Ash actions, the existing Purchase lock and one immutable claim epoch.

EXTEND Commerce's existing Ash resource and sole claim with integration guards and SQL scope constraints. Reuse Plug.Crypto authenticated encryption as in MFA, with associated data for exactly this attempt, reference and claim. AshCloak was considered. The explicit owner boundary supplies per-attempt authenticated data without another vault or dependency. Signals, Temporal Resources and async dispatch do not fit the synchronous one-owner operation.

prohibited_shortcuts.summary: Exclude missing-reference replay, overlapping sends, stale setup cancellation and imported Store business Domains. Initialize evidence alone cannot authorize replacement, cancellation, payment or entitlement.

proof_limitations: HIGH proof covers binding, actor authority, request and durable-effect counts, recovery, redaction and migration. Provider reconciliation, browser rendering, financial settlement, entitlement application and release remain separate.
NewYou exercises actual-stack HTTPS against an independently counted local receiver. No external provider operation or empirical PASS follows from this PR.
Standalone Plan has no new unpaid terminality rule. Existing paid or corrected sources remain ineligible. All Assessment and bundle dispatch stays disabled.
